claim: In the matching retail DLL, three Player SP-side helpers form one caller-connected family around the already-closed Player.AddSP method. Player.ConsumeSP (0x06004ED1) has one Float32 parameter named sp and an exact 51-byte body: it requires MatchMain.inst to convert true, MatchMain.isTimeCounting to be nonzero, and MatchMain.isMatchEnd to be zero, then calls AddSP with the negated input. Player.RecoverSP (0x06004ED2) has one Float32 parameter named sp and an exact 100-byte body: when MatchMain.inst converts true it requires isTimeCounting and not isMatchEnd, while a missing MatchMain proceeds directly; it selects WrestlerParam.spRecovery_Bleeding when isBleeding is set and WrestlerParam.spRecovery otherwise, multiplies the input by Player.SpHealTbl at that raw index, stores the product back into the argument slot, and calls AddSP. Player.InvokeUkeBonus (0x06004ED3) is parameterless with an exact 144-byte body: it returns if isInvokedUkeBonus is already set, otherwise sets it, calls AddSP after integer-dividing UkeRecoveryPoint by 2 and converting to Float32, resets UkeBonusTime to zero, then adds 1800 once for each strict UkeRecoveryPoint threshold exceeded: 7680, 15360, and 30720. FACT-0018 pins ConsumeSP(4.0f); FACT-0020 pins InvokeUkeBonus plus its ConsumeSP/RecoverSP calls; FACT-0027 pins the AddSP callee body used by all three.
